correctness.rationale: All-degree proof: signed-Jordan step representation reduces BV norm to one-sided jumps; step image equals a beta CDF; integrated discrepancy equals beta absolute deviation; convexity and reflection yield attained finite maximum; incomplete-beta integration gives exact binomial expression; beta CLT, bounded second moments and uniqueness of p=1/2 give sharp Gaussian limit and localization. Exact polynomial checker independently confirms degrees 1–16.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2015 Stancu-Bernstein primary theorem is pointwise, whereas the present object is the exact global integrated BV-to-L1 error norm for the ordinary Bernstein operator, with attaining steps and a sharp Gaussian localization result. The 2025 general positive-operator full text likewise establishes local pointwise bounds, and the 2017 result proves variation diminution. Published Bernstein refinement and sampling records concern non-equivalent operators or seminorms; a historical-priority uncertainty remains for uninspected 1983 and 2014 papers.

value.rationale: The global BV-to-L1 approximation error for foundational Bernstein sampling is an independently motivated and natural operator invariant, not the variation of the output itself. Exact finite constants, attaining discontinuities and sharp Gaussian scaling provide operational error calibration and identify the asymptotically worst jump location; this is not an arbitrary parameter slice or merely a rephrased known upper bound.
